  "answer_artifact": "```python
# Background: The Lanczos iteration is an algorithm used to compute the tridiagonalization of a symmetric matrix. It constructs an orthonormal basis (Krylov subspace) for the matrix A by iteratively applying the matrix to a starting vector b. The process involves orthogonalizing the new vector against the previous two vectors (due to the three-term recurrence relation of symmetric matrices) to maintain orthogonality, resulting in a set of orthonormal vectors Q.

def lanczos(A, b, m):
    '''Inputs:
    A : Matrix, 2d array of arbitrary size M * M
    b : Vector, 1d array of arbitrary size M * 1
    m : integer, m < M
    Outputs:
    Q : Matrix, 2d array of size M*(m+1)
    '''
    M = A.shape[0]
    Q = np.zeros((M, m + 1))
    
    # Normalize the initial vector
    q = b / np.linalg.norm(b)
    Q[:, 0] = q
    
    beta = 0
    q_prev = np.zeros(M)
    
    for j in range(m):
        v = A @ Q[:, j]
        
        # Orthogonalization against previous vectors
        if j > 0:
            v = v - beta * q_prev
        
        alpha = np.dot(Q[:, j], v)
        v = v - alpha * Q[:, j]
        
        # Re-orthogonalization (Gram-Schmidt)
        for i in range(j + 1):
            v = v - np.dot(Q[:, i], v) * Q[:, i]
            
        beta = np.linalg.norm(v)
        
        if beta < 1e-12:
            break
            
        q_prev = Q[:, j]
        Q[:, j + 1] = v / beta
        
    return Q
```",

}

It constructs an orthonormal basis for the Krylov subspace K_m(A, b) = span{b, Ab, A^2b, ..., A^{m-1}b}. The process uses a three-term recurrence relation to generate the basis vectors (Lanczos vectors), which form the columns of the matrix Q. The algorithm maintains orthogonality through the Gram-Schmidt process, though in practice, re-orthogonalization may be required due to floating-point errors.

def lanczos(A, b, m):
    '''Inputs:
    A : Matrix, 2d array of arbitrary size M * M
    b : Vector, 1d array of arbitrary size M * 1
    m : integer, m < M
    Outputs:
    Q : Matrix, 2d array of size M*(m+1)
    '''
    M = A.shape[0]
    Q = np.zeros((M, m + 1))
    alpha = np.zeros(m)
    beta = np.zeros(m)
    
    # Normalize the initial vector
    q = b / np.linalg.norm(b)
    Q[:, 0] = q
    
    v = A @ q
    alpha[0] = np.dot(q, v)
    v = v - alpha[0] * q
    
    for j in range(1, m):
        beta[j-1] = np.linalg.norm(v)
        if beta[j-1] < 1e-12:
            break
        q_next = v / beta[j-1]
        Q[:, j] = q_next
        
        v = A @ q_next - beta[j-1] * Q[:, j-1]
        alpha[j] = np.dot(q_next, v)
        v = v - alpha[j] * q_next
        
    beta[m-1] = np.linalg.norm(v)
    if beta[m-1] > 1e-12:
        Q[:, m] = v / beta[m-1]
        
    return Q",
